evidence.location: Article 34 — Methods used for sampling, analyses, tests and diagnoses
evidence.text: Article 34 Methods used for sampling, analyses, tests and diagnoses 1. Methods used for sampling and for laboratory analyses, tests and diagnoses during official controls and other official activities shall comply with Union rules establishing those methods or the performance criteria for those methods. 2. In the absence of the Union rules as referred to in paragraph 1, and in the context of official controls and other official activities, official laboratories shall use one of the following methods according to the suitability for their specific analytical, testing and diagnostic needs: (a) available methods complying with relevant internationally recognised rules or protocols including those that the European Committee for Standardisation (CEN) has accepted; or relevant methods developed or recommended by the European Union reference laboratories and validated in accordance with internationally accepted scientific protocols; (b) in the absence of the suitable rules or protocols, as referred to in point (a), methods which comply with relevant rules established at national level, or, if no such rules exist, relevant methods developed or recommended by national reference laboratories and validated in accordance with internationally accepted scientific protocols; or relevant methods developed and validated with inter or intra-laboratory methods validation studies in accordance with internationally accepted scientific protocols. 3. Where laboratory analyses, tests or diagnoses are urgently needed and none of the methods referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article exists, the relevant national reference laboratory or, if no such national reference laboratory exists, any other laboratory designated in accordance with Article 37(1) may use methods other than those

The Commission may, by means of implementing acts, lay down rules on: (a) the methods to be used for sampling and for laboratory analyses, tests and diagnoses; (b) performance criteria, analysis, test or diagnosis parameters, measurement uncertainty and procedures for the validation of those methods; (c) the interpretation of analytical, testing and diagnostic results. evidence.location: Article 57 — Use of the CHED by customs authorities
evidence.text: Article 57 Use of the CHED by customs authorities 1. The placing and handling of consignments of the categories of animals and goods referred to in Article 47(1) under a customs procedure, including the entry or handling in customs warehouses or free zones, shall be subject to the presentation of the CHED by the operator responsible for the consignment to the custom authorities, without prejudice to the exemptions referred to in Article 48 and the rules referred to in Articles 53 and 54. At this stage, the CHED shall have been duly finalised in the IMSOC by the competent authorities of the border control post. 2. Customs authorities shall: (a) not allow the placing of the consignment under a customs procedure different from the one indicated by the competent authorities of the border control post; and (b) without prejudice to the exemptions referred to in Article 48 and the rules referred to in Articles 53 and 54, only allow the release for free circulation of a consignment upon presentation of a duly finalised CHED which confirms that the consignment is in compliance with the applicable rules referred to in Article 1(2). 3. Where a customs declaration is made for a consignment of the categories of animals or goods referred to in Article 47(1) and the CHED is not presented, the customs authorities shall detain the consignment and immediately notify the competent authorities of the border control post. The competent authorities shall take the necessary measures in accordance with Article 66(6).

evidence.location: Article 66 — Measures to be taken in cases of non-compliant consignments entering the Union
evidence.text: Article 66 Measures to be taken in cases of non-compliant consignments entering the Union 1. The competent authorities shall place under official detention any consignment of animals or goods entering the Union which does not comply with the rules referred to in Article 1(2) and shall refuse its entry into the Union. The competent authorities shall isolate or quarantine, as appropriate, any such consignment and the animals belonging to it shall be kept, cared for or treated under appropriate conditions pending any further decision. If possible, the competent authorities shall also take into account the interest of providing special care in respect of certain types of goods. 2. The Commission shall, by means of implementing acts, lay down rules on the practical arrangements for the isolation and quarantine provided for in the second subparagraph of paragraph 1 of this Article. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 145(2). 3. The competent authority shall, as regards the consignment referred to in paragraph 1 order, without delay, the operator responsible for the consignment to: (a) destroy the consignment; (b) re-dispatch the consignment outside the Union in accordance with Article 72(1) and (2); or (c) subject the consignment to special treatment in accordance with Article 71(1) and (2) or to any other measure necessary to ensure compliance with the rules referred to in Article 1(2), and, where appropriate, allocate the consignment for purposes other than those for which it was originally intended. Any action referred to in points (a), (b) and (c) of the first subparagraph shall be performed in compliance with the rules referred to in Article 1(2), including in particular, as regards consignments of

## 1. Short answer

**The supplied snapshot describes controls, but it does not establish which requirements currently apply to this shipment.** If the figs fall within the relevant Annex II entry under the law currently in force, the snapshot lists a **30% frequency for identity and physical checks**. That is **not** a 30% sampling or laboratory-testing rate. [Effd100d7a6]

The snapshot also points to specific mycotoxin sampling and analysis rules and states an official-certificate requirement for Annex II consignments. Current applicability, the shipment’s classification, and several procedural requirements remain unverified.

## 2. Legal basis and relevant conditions

- **Product scope and checks:** The snapshot covers “dried figs; mixtures of nuts or dried fruits containing figs; dried fig paste; dried figs prepared or preserved, including mixtures” and lists “aflatoxins and ochratoxin A.” It gives a **30%** frequency for identity and physical checks for the dried-fig entry; other listed forms or codes may have different frequencies. [Effd100d7a6] The snapshot identifies CN code **0804 20 90** for dried figs, but that does not establish this shipment’s classification. [Effd100d7a6]

- **Sampling and analysis:** Article 3 in the supplied text directs that, for food listed in Annex I or II because of possible mycotoxin contamination, “the sampling and the analyses shall be performed in accordance with Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2782.” [E6755b594ef] The supplied general official-control text also says samples must be taken, handled and labelled to ensure “their legal, scientific and technical validity.” [E89a5746a84; Ec28a37e9c2] The detailed dried-fig sampling plan and analytical procedures are not provided.

- **Certificate:** Article 11 in the supplied snapshot states: “Each consignment of food and feed listed in Annex II shall be accompanied by an official certificate in accordance with the model set out in Annex IV.” [E798e8c5d45] This is conditional on the consignment falling within an applicable Annex II entry. The supplied evidence does not establish whether accompanying laboratory results are required.

- **Detection is not, by itself, a demonstrated exceedance:** The supplied table gives a B1 maximum of **6.0 μg/kg** for dried figs, but no measured concentration is provided. [E84bba6f619] The detection alone therefore does not establish non-compliance or a basis for a shipment-specific measure. The applicable product category and intended use also require confirmation before assessing compliance.

## 3. Uncertainties / verification needed

**Critical uncovered issues**

- **Current law and shipment facts —** Verify the present-day Annex II listing, scope, and check frequency, and confirm the shipment’s product form and CN/TARIC classification. The supplied snapshot is not proof of current applicability. [Effd100d7a6]
- **Sampling and analysis —** Retrieve the applicable detailed dried-fig sampling and analytical requirements under Regulation (EU) 2023/2782; these are not supplied. [E6755b594ef]
- **Import documentation and process —** Verify whether prior notification, CHED procedures, accompanying analytical results, or other import documentation requirements apply. The supplied evidence does not resolve these questions.
- **Controls and responsibilities —** The applicable general import-control procedures, border-control/CHED process, and competent-authority and food-business-operator responsibilities have not been established by the supplied evidence.
- **Non-compliance measures —** The evidence does not establish the specific measures, consignment decisions, or associated notification or documentation requirements that would apply if a consignment were found non-compliant. The supplied evidence does establish that the cited measures concern consignments found not to comply; detection alone does not establish that condition. [E6297b29035; Ebcbbe77002]
- **Compliance assessment —** Obtain a valid analytical result and verify the applicable product category and intended use before assessing compliance against the maximum level. [E84bba6f619]

**Practical next checks:** Confirm the goods’ form and classification; verify the operative rules and listing, import process, responsibilities, and documentation with the relevant authorities; and obtain a result assessed using the applicable official sampling and analytical procedures.
